speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the consultation. I understand you have had a fever and altered mental status for two days; to help me assess your condition, could you please describe your highest recorded temperature and specifically what changes you or your family have noticed in your level of consciousness?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS)

Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, combined with fever and altered mentation without other common infectious symptoms, I am highly concerned about Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. Can you describe if you have noticed any muscle stiffness, tremors, or changes in your heart rate or blood pressure over the last two days?
